explanation: Compared against Problem 44 of Ben Green's '100 open problems' (p. 22): 'Sieve [N] by removing half the residue classes mod p_i, for primes 2 <= p_1 < ... < p_1000 < N^{9/10}. Does the remaining set have size at most N/10?', with Erdős's remark that the answer is affirmative if all primes are less than N^{1/2}, by the large sieve. The variant has the same setup with p_1000^2 < N in place of the N^{9/10} bound, 'half' read as floor(p_i/2) classes, and conclusion 10·|remaining| <= N. I checked that this is indeed what the large sieve gives: with Q = p_1000 <= √N and only the moduli q = 1 and q = p_i, L >= 1 + 1 + 999·(1/2) > 500 (each odd p contributes (p-1)/(p+1) >= 1/2), so |remaining| <= (N + Q^2)/L < 2N/500 < N/10. The statement is faithful and the solved tag is supported.
